key_concepts: Volcanoes are classified by form, lava characteristics, shape, and eruption type
Shield volcanoes have fluid lava and silent eruptions
Cinder cone volcanoes have less viscous lava and oval cone shape
Composite volcanoes have viscous lava and explosive eruptions
Vulcanian eruptions produce tall umbrella-like eruption clouds
Plinian eruptions can produce eruption columns up to 20 km high
Pelean eruptions produce glowing avalanches called pyroclastic flows
Strombolian eruptions are characterized by lava fountains
Magma with high silica content is more viscous
Magma with less silica content has low viscosity and travels farther
Higher temperature magma flows more easily than lower temperature magma
